statement: The July 2026 feature identifies southern and eastern areas as facing moderate-to-severe drought risk and associated water and livelihood pressure.
compact_statement: The July 2026 feature identifies southern and eastern areas as facing moderate-to-severe drought risk and associated water and livelihood pressure.
uncertainty: Qualitative hazard-map synopsis, not independently verified present crop losses.

statement: UNDP's cited historical assessment reports crop and livestock losses and water scarcity during the 2023–2024 El Niño drought.
compact_statement: UNDP's cited historical assessment reports crop and livestock losses and water scarcity during the 2023–2024 El Niño drought.
uncertainty: Historical assessment summarized by UNDP; no attribution of current violence or 2026 harvest conditions.

statement: FAO identifies smallholders' dependence on rainfed production as a sensitivity to dry spells and changing rainfall.
compact_statement: FAO identifies smallholders' dependence on rainfed production as a sensitivity to dry spells and changing rainfall.
uncertainty: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

statement: The ASIS portal and national drought tool were launched with user training to support hotspot detection and anticipatory decisions.
compact_statement: The ASIS portal and national drought tool were launched with user training to support hotspot detection and anticipatory decisions.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Forestry
uncertainty: Design commitments and intended benefits are not verified outcomes.

statement: The project integrates resilient rural infrastructure, catchment management and risk information into village and municipal planning.
compact_statement: The project integrates resilient rural infrastructure, catchment management and risk information into village and municipal planning.
uncertainty: Undated implementer reporting; intended final coverage and reported achievements differ.

statement: UNDP reports roads, irrigation and water-supply works across six target municipalities, plus local-company employment and reforestation.
compact_statement: UNDP reports roads, irrigation and water-supply works across six target municipalities, plus local-company employment and reforestation.
uncertainty: Reported outputs with no update date; not an independent assessment of sustained resilience or peace outcomes.

statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: Participants reported rainy-season landslides and floods destroying farms in Saburai, Tapo-Memo, Gildapil and Lebos (Bobonaro); Gildapil participants described hunger after maize loss.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: Participants reported rainy-season landslides and floods destroying farms in Saburai, Tapo-Memo, Gildapil and Lebos (Bobonaro); Gildapil participants described hunger after maize loss.
institutions: Institute for Peace, Conflict and Social Studies, UNTL

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 35, ‘Climate and food security’; community account from Gildapil, Bobonaro.

uncertainty: Qualitative participant accounts; no event attribution or prevalence estimate.

statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: In RAEOA, wet-season landslides in Bene-Ufe damaged roads, settlements and farms; flooding and landslides displaced 280 families around Nibin, Usitaqueno, in 2021.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: In RAEOA, wet-season landslides in Bene-Ufe damaged roads, settlements and farms; flooding and landslides displaced 280 families around Nibin, Usitaqueno, in 2021.
institutions: Institute for Peace, Conflict and Social Studies, UNTL

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 22, ‘Environmental security’, RAEOA community findings.

uncertainty: Retrospective, qualitative assessment; not a municipality-wide estimate.

statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: The report describes disputes over water, land and livestock; at Tapo-Memo, unequal irrigation access to the shared Malibaka River raised concern about possible future water conflict.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: The report describes disputes over water, land and livestock; at Tapo-Memo, unequal irrigation access to the shared Malibaka River raised concern about possible future water conflict.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 18–19, ‘Community security’, Tapo-Memo and cross-community resource disputes.

uncertainty: Reported disputes and prospective cross-border water concerns, not attributed to climate. Do not infer climate causation from nearby flood evidence.

statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: Communities reportedly protected 80 water resources in RAEOA; Usi Taqueno residents fenced and cleaned springs, while Saburai protected water distribution through tara bandu.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-02 reports: Communities reportedly protected 80 water resources in RAEOA; Usi Taqueno residents fenced and cleaned springs, while Saburai protected water distribution through tara bandu.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 37–38, ‘Pathways to resilience’, environmental security examples.

uncertainty: Community practices are reported, not independently evaluated for sustained impact.

statement: Source dated 2025-08 reports: The WASH climate assessment says all municipalities face flood exposure; the largest numbers exposed to extreme floods are in Bobonaro and Dili, followed by Ainaro and Baucau.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-08 reports: The WASH climate assessment says all municipalities face flood exposure; the largest numbers exposed to extreme floods are in Bobonaro and Dili, followed by Ainaro and Baucau.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 25, flood exposure discussion under ‘Impacts on communities’.

uncertainty: Underlying exposure-data vintage and municipal denominators are not restated in this passage.

statement: Source dated 2025-08 reports: The assessment expects drought and extreme rainfall to worsen water insecurity, heighten competition and lengthen women’s trips to collect water, with unsafe sources increasing disease risk.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-08 reports: The assessment expects drought and extreme rainfall to worsen water insecurity, heighten competition and lengthen women’s trips to collect water, with unsafe sources increasing disease risk.
scenario: Qualitative drought and extreme-rainfall risk narrative; no emissions scenario specified.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 4 and 26, summary and ‘Impacts on communities’ sections.

uncertainty: Risk narrative, not measured future outcomes; no named municipality is given for this pathway.

statement: The 2025 WASH climate rationale cites 2017 ACAPS material on water competition and disputes within a broader discussion of drought risk.
compact_statement: The 2025 WASH climate rationale cites 2017 ACAPS material on water competition and disputes within a broader discussion of drought risk.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 26, water-competition discussion and citation to ACAPS (2017).

uncertainty: Dated secondary citation from an anticipatory assessment; not a current named violence finding or an isolated causal drought effect.

statement: Source dated 2025-07-04 reports: UNICEF reports community catchment-management expansion to 35 additional sub-villages in Ainaro and Viqueque, implemented by 70 trained residents and nearly 350 other community members, including women and youth.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-07-04 reports: UNICEF reports community catchment-management expansion to 35 additional sub-villages in Ainaro and Viqueque, implemented by 70 trained residents and nearly 350 other community members, including women and youth.
uncertainty: Annual programme reporting; activities are not an independent resilience evaluation.

statement: Source dated 2025-07-04 reports: The 532 built nature-based structures (45 ponds, 313 terraces and 174 check dams) were reported to retain at least 12,567 m³ in one rainfall event; dry-season replenishment is expected, not measured.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-07-04 reports: The 532 built nature-based structures (45 ponds, 313 terraces and 174 check dams) were reported to retain at least 12,567 m³ in one rainfall event; dry-season replenishment is expected, not measured.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 39, infrastructure outputs and expected dry-season water pathway.

uncertainty: Reported retention during one rainfall event; expected dry-season replenishment is not measured persistence.

statement: Source dated 2024-03-27 reports: Sixteen early-warning devices were handed to DNMG; disaster committees were supported in Dili sucos. The article says 15 PREPARADU sucos but lists 16, including six Maloa sites: Villa Verde, Motael, Colmera, Campo Alor, Bairo Pite and Dare.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-03-27 reports: Sixteen early-warning devices were handed to DNMG; disaster committees were supported in Dili sucos. The article says 15 PREPARADU sucos but lists 16, including six Maloa sites: Villa Verde, Motael, Colmera, Campo Alor, Bairo Pite and Dare.

source_refs.locator: Article paragraphs on PREPARADU/Maloa project locations and the 16-station system handover.

uncertainty: Descriptive reporting; the listed PREPARADU suco count is internally inconsistent.

statement: The June 2024 EU/Mercy Corps close-out account reports 537 households with improved shock-preparation capacity, 1,284 people with climate-resilience knowledge and 68 mitigation/adaptation works in the Maloa watershed.
compact_statement: The June 2024 EU/Mercy Corps close-out account reports 537 households with improved shock-preparation capacity, 1,284 people with climate-resilience knowledge and 68 mitigation/adaptation works in the Maloa watershed.

source_refs.locator: Close-out account paragraphs describing household, business and infrastructure results in the Maloa watershed.

uncertainty: Implementer-reported capacity and outputs, not an independent evaluation of losses prevented or peace effects.
